title: Passport data vault and airline submission client
name: Passport data submission

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code protects passport numbers at rest or in transit? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A stored passport ciphertext for booking BK-1 is copied into the row for booking BK-2. What happens when the supplier client submits BK-2?
choices: The BK-1 passport number is sent for BK-2
decrypt() throws during authentication because the booking id is part of the AAD, so nothing is sent
decrypt() returns an empty string and the supplier rejects the request
needsRotation() returns true and the value is re-encrypted for BK-2

questions.prompt: Encrypting the same passport number twice for the same booking produces:
choices: Identical strings, so the column can be used for equality lookups
Identical ciphertext bodies but different key ids
Strings that differ only in the auth tag
Different strings, because each call draws a new random IV

questions.prompt: The supplier's server stops responding mid-request. How does submitPassengerData() behave?
choices: After timeoutMs of socket inactivity the request is destroyed and the promise rejects with a timeout error
It waits indefinitely because keepAlive sockets have no timeout
It resolves with undefined once the socket closes
It retries on another of the 20 pooled sockets
